gloss: to cultivate; to foster; to nurture

definitions.gloss: to cultivate; to foster; to nurture
definitions.explanation: to develop or nurture qualities, skills, or relationships over time

examples.japanese: {信頼|しんらい}を{培|つちか}う。
{長年|ながねん}{培|つちか}ってきた{技術|ぎじゅつ}がある。
examples.english: There are skills cultivated over many years.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{感性|かんせい}を{培|つちか}うことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to nurture children's sensitivity.

notes:
{培|つちか}う means to develop something gradually over time, typically abstract qualities.

VERB TYPE:
- Godan verb (う-verb)
- Transitive

ETYMOLOGY:
- {土|つち} (soil) + {飼|か}う (to raise)
- Originally meant agricultural cultivation
- Now primarily figurative

KANJI NOTE:
- Uses {培|つちか}う (cultivate)
- Related to {栽培|さいばい} (cultivation)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {信頼|しんらい}を{培|つちか}う (cultivate trust)
- {技術|ぎじゅつ}を{培|つちか}う (cultivate skills)
- {感性|かんせい}を{培|つちか}う (nurture sensitivity)
- {友情|ゆうじょう}を{培|つちか}う (foster friendship)
- {関係|かんけい}を{培|つちか}う (nurture relationships)
- {力|ちから}を{培|つちか}う (develop ability)

USAGE NOTES:
- Almost always used figuratively
- Implies gradual, patient development
- Positive connotation
- Often used with ～てきた to emphasize the process over time

SIMILAR VERBS:
- {育|そだ}てる (to raise, grow)
- {養|やしな}う (to nurture, support)
- {磨|みが}く (to polish, refine)

DIFFERENCE FROM SIMILAR VERBS:
- {培|つちか}う: Emphasizes gradual development over time
- {育|そだ}てる: More general raising/growing
- {養|やしな}う: Includes sense of providing sustenance

REGISTER: Somewhat formal. Common in written Japanese and speeches.
